claims.claim: Equinix sits between compute/network demand and physical power/cooling/interconnection infrastructure; rising cabinet power density makes electricity delivery and thermal capacity successor bottlenecks to customer demand.

Record bookings/interconnections and roughly 78% cabinet utilization support structural demand, while the causal constraint is the ability to energize and cool incremental capacity in constrained markets.

risks.risk: Power or cooling delays can strand demand before it becomes revenue-producing capacity.

unknowns.unknown: The evidence does not isolate AI's incremental economics from broader cloud/network demand.

claims.claim: Strong bookings and interconnection additions are compatible with a constrained-capacity thesis; they do not prove that all demand can be served on schedule or at attractive incremental returns.
The present challenge is infrastructure conversion risk rather than demand falsification: high-density workloads increase dependence on utilities, cooling and construction execution.

risks.risk: Capital intensity and utility dependency can delay returns even when customer demand remains strong.
Alternative deployment architectures or locations can redirect incremental workloads if constrained metros cannot add power economically.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not quantify incremental return on capital for AI-density capacity separately from the broader portfolio.
